title: Generic algebraicity in a localized affine model
statement: Let $g:Z\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $s\in S$, and choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ containing $s$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Z$ with $g(U)\subseteq V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ represent $s$, put $B=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pB$ and $C=A\otimes_R B$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Assume that for every generic point $\eta$ of every irreducible component of $Z$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components], the residue extension $\kappa(g(\eta))\subseteq\kappa(\eta)$ is algebraic (every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over the smaller field) [def-weil-residue-field]. Then $A$ is a finite type $R$-algebra and $C$ is a finite type $B$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]; $B$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, its residue field identifies with $\kappa(s)$, and $A\to C$ is localization at the image of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$; the canonical map $B\to\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is an isomorphism; and $\operatorname{Spec}C\cong U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}B$ with its canonical projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. Moreover, for every minimal prime $Q'$ of $C$ (a prime containing no strictly smaller prime), its contraction $Q$ to $A$ is a minimal prime disjoint from the image of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $Q'=QC$, and, writing $q_0=Q\cap R$ and $q=Q'\cap B$, one has $q=q_0B$ and $q_0\subseteq\mathfrak p$. The canonical isomorphisms $\kappa(Q)\cong\kappa(Q')$ and $\kappa(q_0)\cong\kappa(q)$ commute with the induced residue-field maps, and $\kappa(q)\subseteq\kappa(Q')$ is algebraic. No Noetherian or dimension hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, label lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1, proof of condition (2), localization paragraph; affine-local generic-point and minimal-prime transfer made explicit (returned proof steps 1–4).

proof.text: Write $\varphi:R\to A$ for the chart map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the given affine pair $(U,V)$: $A=R[a_1,\ldots,a_n]$ for finitely many $a_i$. Every pure tensor in $C$ is a $B$-linear combination of monomials in $a_i\otimes1$, because its first factor is a polynomial in the $a_i$. Sums of pure tensors give all of $C$, so $C=B[a_1\otimes1,\ldots,a_n\otimes1]$. This proves both finite-type assertions.

source.place: Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, (1) implies (2); finite generators after tensoring are written out.

proof.text: Put $T=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $W=\varphi(T)\subset A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with base ring and algebra both $R$, multiplicative set $T$, module $M=R$ and module $N=A$. It identifies $B\otimes_R A$ with $T^{-1}A$ as modules, taking $(r/t)\otimes a$ to $\varphi(r)a/\varphi(t)$. Flip the tensor factors to obtain $C\to W^{-1}A$, $a\otimes(r/t)\mapsto a\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$. This is multiplicative and sends $1$ to $1$, as checked on pure tensors; its inverse is $a/\varphi(t)\mapsto(a\otimes1)(1\otimes(1/t))$. Thus $A\to C$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, satisfies the three localization properties of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso]. This also covers $0\in W$, when both rings are zero.

source.place: Tag 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization: apply to the R-module A, with tensor symmetry; the multiplicative formula is checked explicitly.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $B$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pB$ and residue field $\kappa_R(\mathfrak p)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] to $(S,V,s)$. Its canonical isomorphism is $B\to\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $r/t\mapsto r_s/t_s$; it identifies maximal ideals and hence identifies $B/\mathfrak m$ with $\kappa(s)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] to $R\to A$ and $R\to B$. Its inverse gives $\operatorname{Spec}C\cong U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}B$, and the two projections are induced by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, as required.

Let $Q'$ be a minimal prime of $C$ and let $Q$ be its contraction to $A$. The prime correspondence in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso](1), applied to step 2, gives $Q\cap W=\emptyset$ and $Q'=QC$. If $P\subseteq Q$ is any prime of $A$, it too avoids $W$, so the same correspondence gives a prime $PC\subseteq QC=Q'$. Minimality gives $PC=Q'$, and contraction then gives $P=Q$. Thus $Q$ is minimal in $A$. Put $q_0=\varphi^{-1}(Q)$ and $q=(B\to C)^{-1}(Q')$. The tensor square commutes, so the contraction of $q$ to $R$ is $q_0$. Since $Q$ avoids $W$, $q_0$ avoids $T$, equivalently $q_0\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Apply the same prime correspondence to $R\to B=T^{-1}R$: $q=q_0B$.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization: contraction and extension are inverse, with inclusion preserved by extension.

proof.text: The component theorem [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] makes $V(Q)$ an irreducible component of $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The closure of $\{Q\}$ in $U$ is $V(Q)$: a closed $V(I)$ contains $Q$ exactly when $I\subseteq Q$. Let $\eta$ be this point in $Z$, and put $D=\overline{\{\eta\}}$ in $Z$. The closure of a singleton is irreducible, and $D\cap U=V(Q)$. If an irreducible closed subset $E\subseteq Z$ contains $D$, then $E\cap U$ is nonempty, open in $E$, irreducible and dense in $E$. Indeed any two nonempty relatively open subsets of an irreducible space meet, which proves both irreducibility and density of a nonempty open subset. Maximality of $V(Q)$ inside $U$ forces $E\cap U=V(Q)$, and density yields $E=\overline{E\cap U}=\overline{V(Q)}=D$. Consequently $D$ is an irreducible component of $Z$ and $\eta$ is its generic point. This argument does not require a finite or locally finite component family.

source.place: Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible, (1) and (3); extension of the component through an open chart is proved from irreducibility.

proof.text: Let $y=g(\eta)$. Its prime on $V$ is $q_0$: the map of affine spectra sends a prime to its contraction. The germ isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identify $\mathcal O_{S,y}$ with $R_{q_0}$ and $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ with $A_Q$. Under these identifications the stalk map of $g$ sends $r/t$ to $\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$, since it sends a section germ $r_y$ to the germ $\varphi(r)_\eta$ and preserves inverses. Taking quotients by maximal ideals therefore identifies the residue extension $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(\eta)$ with $\kappa_R(q_0)\to\kappa_A(Q)$, by [def-weil-residue-field]. The hypothesis applies to the generic point produced in step 5, so this last extension is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, (6), and Tag 01HB, definition-locally-ringed-space: compute the stalk map on section germs and inverses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso](3) to $A\to C$ and to $R\to B$. It gives field isomorphisms $\alpha:\kappa_A(Q)\to\kappa_C(Q')$ and $\beta:\kappa_R(q_0)\to\kappa_B(q)$ induced by the localization maps. If $h$ and $h'$ denote the residue maps before and after localization, then $\alpha h=h'\beta$: on the class of $r/t\in R_{q_0}$ both sides are the class of $(\varphi(r)\otimes1)/(\varphi(t)\otimes1)$ in $\kappa_C(Q')$. Such classes represent every element of $\kappa_R(q_0)$, so this proves the full square commutes. Given $z\in\kappa_C(Q')$, choose a nonzero polynomial $\sum_i c_iX^i$ over $\kappa_R(q_0)$ annihilating $\alpha^{-1}(z)$, by step 6. Then $\sum_i\beta(c_i)X^i$ is nonzero, since $\beta$ is injective, and annihilates $z$ by the square. Hence $\kappa_B(q)\to\kappa_C(Q')$ is algebraic. All clauses are proved without a Noetherian or dimension assumption.
